title: Addressing Unmeasured Confounder for Recommendation with Sensitivity Analysis

problem.claim: Recommendation requires estimating the causal effect of recommending an item on user feedback.

gap.claim: Existing methods may ignore unmeasured confounders, producing biased propensities and harming recommendation performance.

contributions.claim: The work addresses the risk of unmeasured confounders in recommender systems.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems need to estimate the causal effect of recommendations on user feedback.
Estimating this effect generally requires blocking confounders that affect both recommendation and feedback.
Propensity can be incorporated into model learning to mitigate confounding bias.
Existing methods can overlook unmeasured confounders, leading to biased propensities and worse recommendation performance.
The work targets the risk posed by unmeasured confounders in recommender systems.

source_observation.claim: Unmeasured variables affecting both recommendation and feedback can bias propensity estimates and hurt performance.

interpretation.claim: Causal recommendation methods should assess sensitivity to confounding that is not observed.

application.claim: Recommendation pipelines can include explicit checks for how unmeasured confounders might alter estimated effects or performance.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify which sensitivity-analysis procedure, assumptions, or evaluation settings are used.

unknowns: The abstract units do not specify the proposed sensitivity-analysis method.
The abstract units do not report experiments, datasets, quantitative results, or assumptions.
